definitions.explanation: Describes someone who has recently entered or joined an organization, school, or group. Almost always used as a modifier before another noun.

examples.japanese: {新入|しんにゅう}{社員|しゃいん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{研修|けんしゅう}→研修：05322_kenshuu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{始|はじ}まった→始まる：00841_hajimaru⟧。
examples.english: The training for new employees has started.

examples.japanese: {新入|しんにゅう}{生|せい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歓迎|かんげい}する→歓迎する：26997_kangeisuru⟧⟦パーティー→パーティー：02946_paatii⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|ひら}いた→開く：01979_hiraku⟧。
examples.english: We held a party to welcome the new students.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今年|ことし}→今年：00722_kotoshi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{新入|しんにゅう}⟦{部員|ぶいん}→部員：27409_buin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{去年|きょねん}→去年：00727_kyonen⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{多|おお}く→多い：01127_ooi⟧、⟦{活気|かっき}→活気：02554_kakki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: This year's new club members are more numerous than last year, and there's a lot of energy.

notes:
{新入|しんにゅう} means newly entering or newly joined. It is used almost exclusively as a prefix modifying another noun — it rarely stands alone.

COMPOUNDS:
- {新入|しんにゅう}{社員|しゃいん}: new employee (often abbreviated {新入|しんにゅう}{社員|しゃいん} → {新社員|しんしゃいん})
- {新入|しんにゅう}{生|せい}: new student (entering a school)
- {新入|しんにゅう}⟦{部員|ぶいん}→部員：27409_buin⟧: new club member
- {新入|しんにゅう}⟦{会員|かいいん}→会員：02535_kaiin⟧: new member (of an organization)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {新入|しんにゅう}: newly joined (prefix, always modifies a noun)
- ⟦{新人|しんじん}→新人：02500_shinjin⟧: newcomer, rookie (can stand alone as a noun)
- ⟦{入社|にゅうしゃ}→入社：03131_nyuusha⟧: joining a company (the act itself)

SEASONAL CONTEXT:
In Japan, the school and fiscal year begin in April. {新入|しんにゅう}{生|せい} and {新入|しんにゅう}{社員|しゃいん} are most commonly heard in spring.
